text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time, saying,
Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh, and announce to it the message I am giving you.
So this time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, just as the LORD had told him. Nineveh was an enormous city, requiring three days just to walk across it.
Jonah started into the city, walking a single day's distance, and proclaimed, In forty more days, Nineveh will be overthrown!
And the people of Nineveh believed God. They called for a fast and dressed themselves in sackcloth, everyone from the most important down to the least.
When word reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat down in the ashes.
Then he sent out this proclamation through the city, by order of the king and his officials: No person or animal, herd or flock, is to eat anything or to drink water.
Instead, every person and animal must be covered in sackcloth. Let everyone call out earnestly to God and turn back from their evil ways and from the violence they practice.
Who can say? Perhaps God will change his mind and relent, turning from his burning anger, so that we do not perish.
When God saw what they did — that they had turned from their evil ways — he relented and did not bring on them the disaster he had threatened.
